title: Prepared-result handoff — intrinsic send vs Isolate.exit (measurement)
impact: Experiment A of the peer's estimand split (exp 241 confound, exp 244 = the pool-capacity half): measures the INTRINSIC transfer estimand — `SendPort.send` vs `Isolate.exit` for a given result graph, with spawn/SQLite/decode/construction all outside the timed interval. Prepared-result barrier protocol: a worker builds the real production ResultSet (flat values list + RowSchema + wrapper) and holds it; main records t0 (Go sent) and t1 (received, first op in handler); handoffWall = t1-t0, both on main (one clock). ONE fresh PROCESS per observation (no heap accumulation / mode carryover — the exact confounds exp 241 suffered), ABBA blocks, empty-envelope control isolating fixed overhead. Three mechanistic facts, each isolated: (1) **Isolate.exit has a ~47 us fixed-overhead premium** over send (empty envelope 147 vs 100 us) — its sendability walk + teardown; (2) **strings/immutable leaves are SHARED on send, not copied** — a 400 KB string adds ~0 us (payload -4), a 1 MB string +18 us; send's copy cost tracks the MUTABLE flat-list SLOT COUNT (27 -> 163 -> 636 us at 20k -> 48k -> 200k slots), not payload bytes; (3) **exit is zero-copy**, so it wins once the structural copy exceeds its 47 us premium — **crossover ~48k slots** (num48k exit -22 us; num10kx20 -345 us). Resolution (with exp 244): small-to-moderate (<~48k slots) and ALL string-heavy results are send ≈ exit within the pre-registered equivalence margin (39-71 us diffs) — the middle is a declared wash, slight lean to send; large structural (>~48k slots) materially favors exit; the current sacrifice policy's intent is validated. The one real defect is the TRIGGER: sacrifice fires on BYTES, but the cost driver is mutable slot count, so a large STRING (400 KB, 1 slot, shared free) is send-favored (96 vs 167 us) yet wrongly sacrificed at 256 KB bytes — the text/shared-leaf misroute, now confirmed intrinsically. Ships no runtime change; actionable follow-up is a slot-count/shared-leaf sacrifice guard.
